title: Cell Structure & Organelles
description: The main parts of plant and animal cells and what each one does. A solid review for intro biology.
subject: science

cards.definition: Organelle that produces most of the cell's ATP through cellular respiration, often called the powerhouse of the cell.
Membrane-bound organelle that contains the cell's DNA and controls which genes are expressed.
Organelle in plant and algal cells where photosynthesis turns light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar.
Phospholipid bilayer that surrounds the cell and controls what enters and leaves. Also called the plasma membrane.
Rigid layer outside the cell membrane of plants, fungi, and most bacteria that provides support and protection.
Everything inside the cell membrane except the nucleus, including the fluid cytosol and the organelles.
Small structure made of RNA and protein that builds proteins by reading mRNA. Found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells and not surrounded by a membrane.
Network of membranes studded with ribosomes that makes proteins for membranes, for export, or for other organelles.
Network of membranes without ribosomes that makes lipids, helps detoxify drugs, and stores calcium ions.
Stack of flattened membrane sacs that modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids for delivery.
Membrane sac of digestive enzymes that breaks down worn-out organelles, food particles, and engulfed microbes.
Membrane-bound storage sac. Plant cells usually have a large central vacuole that stores water and helps keep the cell firm.
Small membrane-bound sac that carries materials within the cell or to the cell surface.
Network of protein fibers, including microtubules and microfilaments, that gives the cell its shape and helps it move.
Cylinder made of microtubules, found in pairs in animal cells, that helps organize microtubules during cell division.
Dense region inside the nucleus where ribosomal RNA is made and ribosome subunits are assembled.
Double membrane around the nucleus, with nuclear pores that control what passes in and out.
Small organelle with enzymes that break down fatty acids and toxic substances, producing and then breaking down hydrogen peroxide.
Long, whiplike structure that propels a cell, such as a sperm cell, through fluid.
Short, hairlike projections that beat together to move a cell or to sweep fluid across the cell's surface.
A cell with no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles. Bacteria and archaea are prokaryotes.
A cell with a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Plants, animals, fungi, and protists are eukaryotes.
